headline: CISA confirmed that attackers now exploit the Brotli decoder flaw behind Node2Shell as a parallel campaign breached hundreds of Adobe Commerce stores and Japan's GMO Internet Group told Onamae.com customers to shut their computers off ahead of a threatened ransomware attack.

emerging_trends.text: Anthropic said an unreleased model chained browser and kernel flaws into working exploits in its lab on the same day an autonomous system surfaced four long-hidden bugs in the control software that runs particle accelerators, putting machine-speed vulnerability discovery on both sides of the fence.
emerging_trends.topic_title: AI Models Chain Browser and Kernel Flaws Into Exploits

emerging_trends.text: Traffic against the Brotli decompression flaw moved from failed honeypot probes to hundreds of breached online stores inside a week, a reminder that one bug in a bundled library reaches every runtime that ships it.

Kroll found nearly seven in ten people in the breaches it handled lost data a supplier they never chose was holding, the same pattern British police forces and Sony's So-net subscribers lived through this week.

topics.title: Brotli Exploitation Hits Magento Stores
topics.latest_developments: CISA confirmed active exploitation of CVE-2026-111497, the Brotli flaw researchers call Node2Shell, Broccoli2Shell, and HTTP2Shell, and two honeypot operators logged attempts, one of them firing a broken exploit; separately attackers breached hundreds of Adobe Commerce and Magento stores through CVE-2026-48356 in a campaign researchers named PolyShell.
topics.summary: CVE-2026-111497 is an unchecked return value rated 9.2 in Google's Brotli compression library that runs an attacker's code in any application decompressing attacker-supplied Brotli data, among them Node.js, .NET, PowerShell, Bun, and the Python brotli packages. Update the bundling runtime and patch Adobe Commerce and Magento, where CVE-2026-48356 allows an unrestricted file upload.

sources.title: CISA warns of hackers now exploiting critical Node2Shell flaw
CISA Warns of Node2Shell Exploitation as Honeypots Log Attack Attempts

topics.title: AI Models Chain Browser and Kernel Flaws Into Exploits
topics.latest_developments: Anthropic reported that an unreleased model found flaws in Chrome, Safari, Android, Windows, and Linux and chained them into working proof-of-concept exploits in the lab, with every vendor notified and every bug already patched; an autonomous system uncovered four long-hidden flaws in EPICS Base, the control software behind particle accelerators and fusion labs, the worst rated 9.8; and TrendAI dissected three exposed attacker server environments, one of which ran 44 AI agents against organizations in Japan.
topics.summary: EPICS Base releases 7.0.10 and earlier carry CVE-2026-114595 through CVE-2026-114598, which crash processes, corrupt memory, leak data, and may run code; research facilities should upgrade. Defenders should assume attackers operate the same flaw-finding and attack-automation tooling.

topics.title: So-net and the Supplier Breach Chain
topics.latest_developments: Sony Network Communications disclosed that attackers reached the So-net member database and took personal information on more than 2.58 million current and former customers of the Japanese internet provider plus the email passwords of 54,401 users; Kroll's Data Breach Outlook 2026 found nearly seven in ten people in the breaches it handled lost data an outside supplier held; His Majesty's Inspectorate of Constabulary and Fire and Rescue Services reported British police data leaking several times this decade through third-party information technology suppliers; and a card skimming crew hijacked the shared analytics script of the e-commerce platform Convertr to lift shoppers' payment details at checkout.
topics.summary: So-net customers should change email passwords immediately and watch for credential reuse elsewhere. The wider pattern puts the work on vendor inventories: know which suppliers hold your customer records and which third-party scripts load on your checkout pages.

sources.title: Data breach at Sony-owned internet provider compromises 2.6 million customer records
Breach victims discover their data was held by companies they've never heard of

topics.title: Ransomware Affiliate Draws 70 Months
topics.latest_developments: Artem Stryzhak, a 36-year-old Ukrainian national who pleaded guilty last year to running Nefilim and Hive ransomware attacks on hospitals, government bodies, and high-revenue companies between 2018 and 2021, drew 70 months in prison; the Justice Department seized a domain belonging to Virtualine, a bulletproof hosting provider it says carried sexually explicit images of minors and nonconsensual intimate imagery and laundered bitcoin; and prosecutors indicted a Malaysian national after a sting in Madagascar broke up a scam compound operation, part of an action against five foreign nationals.
topics.summary: The three moves land within a day of each other and hit different layers of the criminal economy: an intrusion affiliate, the hosting that shelters criminal services, and the scam-center industry now spreading beyond Southeast Asia. Victims of Nefilim and Hive can expect restitution proceedings to follow.

sources.title: Nefilim, Hive ransomware operator given five-year-plus sentence after guilty plea
Nefilim and Hive ransomware affiliate gets 70 months in prison
FBI Seizes Virtualine Domain Over Alleged Criminal Hosting and Bitcoin Money Laundering
US indicts Malaysian national after Madagascar scam operation uncovered

topics.title: GMO Tells Onamae Customers to Shut Down
topics.latest_developments: GMO Internet Group told Onamae.com Desktop Cloud customers to disconnect from the internet and power down their computers after the intruder who planted malware on as many as 26,739 customer servers threatened to encrypt systems on October 28, 2026, and the company refused the extortion demand and opened a reward program that day paying up to $1 million in total for tips that lead to an arrest or an international wanted notice.
topics.summary: Onamae.com Desktop Cloud hosts Windows desktops that Japanese customers use for foreign exchange trading. Customers should keep those machines offline until GMO clears them, and rotate every credential typed into the hosted desktops.

sources.title: Japan's GMO urges customers to shut down PCs amid ransomware threat
Japan's GMO Offers $1 Million Bounty to Catch Hackers Behind FX Trading Cloud Breach

topics.title: ShinyHunters Chained Three PeopleSoft Flaws
topics.latest_developments: The researchers who reported the Oracle PeopleSoft bug ShinyHunters has exploited since May 2026 said this week it is three flaws chained together, rooted in a server-side request forgery that reaches an internal management interface because PeopleSoft trusts its own loopback address, all of which Oracle patched under the single identifier CVE-2026-35273 in June 2026; attackers meanwhile began probing CVE-2026-101767, an unauthenticated SQL injection in Oracle E-Business Suite that leads to remote code execution.
topics.summary: PeopleSoft operators who skipped the June 2026 Oracle patch remain exposed to the full chain, and E-Business Suite administrators should apply the October 2026 Critical Patch Update now that scanning has started. Both products sit on human resources and financial data.

sources.title: ShinyHunters-Exploited Oracle PeopleSoft Zero-Day Turns Out to Be Three Chained Flaws
Hackers Start Probing Fresh Oracle EBS Vulnerability

business_politics.title: Israel's Election Leaves Neither Bloc a Majority
business_politics.latest_developments: Overnight counting reversed Tuesday's exit polls—Benjamin Netanyahu's results improved as ballots came in and his bloc moved ahead of Gadi Eisenkot's—and the prime minister spent Wednesday urging rivals to join a Jewish coalition that shuts out Arab parties.
business_politics.summary: Partial results from Israel's parliamentary election give Netanyahu more seats than exit polls showed, still short of a 61-seat Knesset majority and short of the number his current coalition holds. Neither camp has a simple path to a government, leaving Israel's direction on Iran, Gaza, and Netanyahu's own legal fate unsettled through coalition talks that could run weeks.

sources.title: Netanyahu Holds on as Election Results Show No Clear Winner
Netanyahu ahead but no clear winner in Israeli election
Israel's election: what happens next?

business_politics.title: Houthis Strike Ras Tanura and Oil Climbs
business_politics.latest_developments: Yemen's Houthi militants said Tuesday they hit Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery in the Eastern Province with a ballistic missile, and crude rose Wednesday morning as traders priced in a wider Middle East escalation.
business_politics.summary: Ras Tanura is Saudi Arabia's largest refinery and sits at the heart of the kingdom's Gulf export complex, so a direct missile hit moves the risk premium in a market already strained by the standoff between Washington and Tehran. Diplomatic effort has failed to persuade traders that the fighting stays contained.

sources.title: Oil Prices Rise as Houthi Militants Target Saudi Energy
Oil Gains As Market Prices in Greater Risk of Mideast Escalation

business_politics.title: The Fed Decides Wednesday
business_politics.latest_developments: Treasury and European government bond yields rose in Wednesday morning trade and gold edged lower as investors positioned for a Federal Reserve decision economists expect to leave rates unchanged, with hyperscaler earnings landing the same day.
business_politics.summary: Technology stocks extended the rally that Anthropic's listing paperwork set off, carrying the market into the Fed's statement and the quarter's biggest earnings day. Big and regional banks alike report a surge in lending tied to artificial-intelligence buildouts, and their executives keep telling investors they remain cautious about it.

Global Government Bond Yields Rise Ahead of Fed Decision, U.K. Budget
AI Boom Drives a Jump in Lending, but Bankers Still Sound Cautious

business_politics.title: Healey Delivers the Budget at 12:30
business_politics.latest_developments: Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey stands up at 12:30 p.m. London time Wednesday with energy costs at the center of his first Budget, sterling already lower against the dollar on the risk the package looks loose, and plans to hand Lancashire and Essex elected mayors as part of Andy Burnham's devolution push.
business_politics.summary: Healey has to cut household energy bills without unsettling gilt investors who have punished every sign of fiscal slippage, after September inflation and £24.5 billion of public borrowing both overshot forecasts. The Financial Times Monetary Policy Radar team expects the Bank of England to open a short, precautionary tightening cycle in November.

business.title: KP Threads Takes a Greensburg Storefront
business.latest_developments: Kelly Pruss, a Greensburg native, has moved her three-year-old branded apparel business, KP Threads, into a storefront at the corner of South Urania and Euclid avenues in her hometown, TribLive reported Wednesday, October 28.
business.summary: Pruss spotted a for-rent sign in the window and took the space for the boutique, which sells branded apparel and had operated without a Greensburg shopfront. The move adds a retail tenant to a Westmoreland County downtown that has worked for years to fill vacant storefronts.

sources.title: Greensburg native moves branded apparel business KP Threads to hometown storefront

business.title: National Operators Dominate Pennsylvania Medical Marijuana
business.latest_developments: TribLive reported Wednesday, October 28, that multistate companies now control most of Pennsylvania's medical marijuana market, a decade after the state legalized it.
business.summary: Former state senator Daylin Leach, who pushed the legalization law through Harrisburg, told the paper he once knew the name of everyone running a dispensary in Pennsylvania. Consolidation matters as the legislature keeps debating adult-use legalization, which would hand the same national operators a far bigger market.

sources.title: National companies dominate Pa.'s medical marijuana market

business.title: Pittsburgh City Paper Turns 35
business.latest_developments: Pittsburgh City Paper published a package Wednesday, October 28, marking 35 years since its 1991 founding, including an accounting of the back-page advertising that paid the bills.
business.summary: The alt-weekly's staff recount a newsroom that doubled as a journalistic proving ground, and one column puts the adult-services ads that ran in the back pages during the 1990s at $15,000 to $20,000 a week, revenue typical of alt-weeklies then. A companion history traces the Pittsburgh Courier and OUT Magazine as the paper's predecessors in the city's alternative press.

sources.title: After 35 years, City Paper's story is still being written — partly by readers like you
City Paper and sex workers were in bed together since the beginning — and it was good for everyone

around_town.title: Federal Monitors Stay Outside Allegheny County Polls
around_town.latest_developments: County officials said Tuesday, October 27, that United States Department of Justice Election Day monitors will not enter any of Allegheny County's more than 1,300 polling places, and Westmoreland County expects no federal monitors at all, narrowing the deployment reported last week.
around_town.summary: Pennsylvania law limits who may stand inside a polling place, so the federal monitors assigned to Allegheny County will work from outside on Tuesday, November 3. The Post-Gazette published its guide to the election the same week, covering where and how to vote and the mail ballot rules.

sources.title: Allegheny, Westmoreland prepare for Election Day as DOJ poll monitors restricted

around_town.title: Tarentum Bridge Rehab Slips to 2028
around_town.latest_developments: TribLive reported Wednesday, October 28, that the three-year rehabilitation of the Tarentum Bridge has moved to 2028, a year later than planned.
around_town.summary: The bridge carries Route 366 over the Allegheny River between Tarentum and New Kensington, and the project will bring extended detours and traffic tangles to Alle-Kiski Valley commuters once it starts. The delay gives drivers an additional year before the closures begin.

sources.title: 3-year Tarentum Bridge rehab project pushed to 2028

around_town.title: Districts Shrug at the New Phone Ban
around_town.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Wednesday, October 28, that several Western Pennsylvania school districts object to Pennsylvania's new bell-to-bell cellphone ban, saying their own policies already keep phones out of classrooms.
around_town.summary: Governor Josh Shapiro signed the statewide ban in Central Bucks on Monday, October 26, and it takes effect with the 2027-28 school year, requiring districts to keep student phones away from bell to bell. A separate state Senate bill would limit artificial intelligence in classrooms to a supporting role behind teachers.

sources.title: Some school districts pan Pennsylvania's new cellphone ban, saying they already have rules
Pennsylvania Senate bill aims to keep teachers, not AI, at forefront of classroom learning

events.title: 'Hadestown' at the Benedum Center
events.latest_developments: TribLive reviewed the touring production of "Hadestown" at the Benedum Center on Wednesday, October 28, calling it an epically great show.
events.summary: The musical retells Greek myth as a road to the underworld and plays the Benedum Center in downtown Pittsburgh's Cultural District. TribLive's reviewer places it among a run of Greek-mythology stagings around the region this year.

sources.title: Stage review: 'Hadestown' at the Benedum Center is an epically great show

events.title: Pitt Jazz Week Puts the Organ Onstage
events.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette previewed the University of Pittsburgh's Jazz Seminar and Concert on Wednesday, October 28, reporting that this year's program centers on an organ summit.
events.summary: The Pitt Jazz Seminar and Concert pairs daytime seminars with an evening concert of visiting players, a format the university has run for decades. This edition builds the lineup around the Hammond organ.

sources.title: Pitt Jazz Seminar and Concert puts the organ in the spotlight

events.title: City Paper Lays Out November
events.latest_developments: Pittsburgh City Paper published its November event guide Wednesday, October 28.
events.summary: The guide runs through a sex-positive film festival, a neighborhood cat crawl, a toddler rave, and a No Doubt cover show, with dates and venues for each listing.

around_teams.title: Heyward's Show Turns to the Browns
around_teams.latest_developments: Cam Heyward and Hayden Walsh posted Wednesday's Not Just Football, their first Browns preview, breaking down Aaron Rodgers' big plays and the red zone defense from the Paris game and knocking the playing surfaces the team found overseas.
around_teams.summary: Heyward's podcast runs through Week 7 against the New Orleans Saints before looking ahead to the Steelers' home game against the Cleveland Browns on Sunday, November 1, at 1 p.m. on CBS, with the two hosts also revealing their Halloween costumes and naming their NFL villains.

around_teams.title: Hiles on the Kordell Stewart Documentary
around_teams.latest_developments: Post-Gazette columnist Noah Hiles wrote Wednesday, October 28, that HBO's new documentary on Kordell Stewart should make Steelers fans uncomfortable.
around_teams.summary: Stewart quarterbacked the Steelers from 1995 to 2002, took them to two AFC championship games, and absorbed years of abuse from the fan base and talk radio. Hiles argues the film puts that treatment back in front of the people who delivered it.

sources.title: Noah Hiles: HBO's Kordell Stewart documentary should be an uncomfortable watch for Steelers fans

team_usa.title: Pulisic Nears a Milan Extension
team_usa.latest_developments: Sources told ESPN on Wednesday, October 28, that Christian Pulisic will sign a new AC Milan contract running through 2031.
team_usa.summary: Pulisic, the captain and leading attacker of the United States men's national team, has become Milan's central forward threat and scored in the club's 2-0 win over Udinese on Sunday, October 25. The deal would keep him in Serie A through the 2030 World Cup cycle.

sources.title: Sources: Pulisic set to sign new AC Milan contract

team_usa.title: Eddie Johnson Takes In the Florida Three-Year-Old
team_usa.latest_developments: Former United States men's national team forward Eddie Johnson said Monday, October 26, that his academy will train the three-year-old boy whom a Florida youth soccer program removed last weekend after tensions over the child's play.
team_usa.summary: Johnson scored 19 goals in 63 appearances for the United States and now runs a youth academy. His offer followed a weekend in which police were called to the Florida youth program over the dispute.

sources.title: Ex-USMNT star Johnson to train 3-year-old removed from Florida soccer game
